[[File:DarthMaladi-LECG.jpg|thumb|right|250px|[[Darth Maladi]], [[Gender/Legends|female]] [[Devaronian/Legends|Devaronian]] member of the [[One Sith]], was skilled at bioengineering.]]
{{Quote|What's that armor made from?"<br />"Not made. Bioengineered. A living vonduun crab, and technology is a poor second to it.|[[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]] and [[Nom Anor]]|<ref name="Boba Fett: A Practical Man">''[[Boba Fett: A Practical Man]]''</ref>}}
'''Bioengineering''', also known as '''genetic engineering''', was the process of altering or adapting biological subjects to suit specific needs. Those who engaged in these activities were known as '''bioengineers''' (sometimes hyphenated '''bio-engineer'''). Various companies and organizations took part in bioengineering, such as the [[Republic Livestock and Agriculture Administration]], genetic research industries such as [[GeneSculpt]] and [[TheraGene]], and entire planetary governments such as the [[Arkanian Dominion]].

==History==
The earliest example of bioengineering was countless years ago on the sentient planet [[Yuuzhan'tar]], which modified living organisms on its surface for specific uses. The living planetoid used these organisms and its symbionts the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] to fight off threats to their world. Eventually, Yuuzhan'tar was destroyed but the Yuuzhan Vong retained the practice of bioengineering complex organisms which was done so by their [[Shaper caste|Shapers]] in order to suit set tasks usually accomplished through technology. This was partly because of the intense technophobia the Yuuzhan Vong had toward machines and they termed their living servants as [[biot]]s.

The [[Qella]] were another race that had mastered bioengineering by modifying organisms on their world, though they did not develop the means to mass produce the creatures. By [[120 BBY]], they produced the [[Teljkon Vagabond]] and launched it from their world in order to reform [[Brath Qella]] after its surface was devastated by a planetoid. Later, by [[129 BBY]], the [[Langhesi]] had migrated to the planet [[Zonama Sekot/Legends|Zonama Sekot]], where they began shaping the native lifeforms to produce living technology through bioengineering. Certain other species that had learned the art of bioengineering included the [[Lurrian]]s, who had genetically engineered a number of species on their home planet of [[Lur]]. The planet [[Gallinore]] in the [[Hapes Consortium/Legends|Hapes Consortium]] also had experience in bioengineering as they created the [[Rainbow gem]] in laboratories. The [[Charon/Legends|Charon]] were another species that used bioengineering to create living technology, and their bioscientist caste were adept in its usage.

By [[21 BBY/Legends|21 BBY]], the [[Confederacy of Independent Systems/Legends|Confederacy of Independent Systems]] had conducted their own bioengineering procedures, which they worked on the planet [[Xagobah/Legends|Xagobah]]. The [[Techno Union/Legends|Techno Union]] were thus able to bioengineer [[Malvil-tree]]s and created a living structure called the [[Mazariyan]] Citadel on the planet. It was involved in the [[Battle of Xagobah (Clone Wars)|Battle of Xagobah]] during the Clone Wars. Following the Clone Wars, the newly formed [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] placed strict laws on both [[Cloning/Legends|cloning]] technology and bioengineering, which impacted on the Lurrians. The rigid laws also led to numerous acts to circumvent them, such as the kidnapping of Lurrians in order to make use of their talents. The [[Imperial Corps of Bioengineers/Legends|Imperial Corps of Bioengineers]] was the accordant department of the Empire during the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]], the Empire bioengineered the [[cliff wampa]] from the original [[Wampa/Legends|wampa]] ice creature native to the [[Planet/Legends|planet]] [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]. In addition, Imperial scientists were involved in the creation of bioengineered creatures such as [[Subject 4D668493X]].

==Examples of Bioengineering==
*The cloners of [[Kamino/Legends|Kamino]] modified the [[Clone trooper/Legends|clone troopers]]' loyalty, aggression, independence and discipline in order to guarantee that the army would be more docile and less independent than their template.<ref name="Republic Commando: Triple Zero">''[[Republic Commando: Triple Zero]]''</ref>
*The [[Nightseer]], [[Wingle]], and [[Craw-maw]] of [[Ruan]] were all modified by food corporations in order to be wingless and silent.<ref name="The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse">''[[The New Jedi Order: Agents of Chaos II: Jedi Eclipse]]''</ref>
*The [[Ragithian Human]]s of [[Ragith III]] were genetically altered to be larger and stronger than normal humans to withstand their planet's gravity.<ref name="Death Star novel">[[Death Star (novel)|''Death Star'']]</ref>
*The [[Gra]] was genetically modified to be a hardier herd animal.<ref name="Dark Forces: Rebel Agent">''[[Dark Forces: Rebel Agent]]''</ref>
*The [[Shistavanen/Legends|Shistavanen]] were bioengineered as a part of their evolutionary process.<ref name="The New Essential Guide to Alien Species">''[[The New Essential Guide to Alien Species]]''</ref>
*[[Seventeen]] was a unique bioengineered creature composed of parts of several different animals.<ref name="The Clone Wars: Act on Instinct">''[[The Clone Wars: Act on Instinct]]''</ref>
*[[Stone mite/Legends|Stone mites]] were an engineered crustacean that fed specifically on metals.<ref>{{HoloNetNewsWeb|55|regional/1359_3.html|Stone Mites Claim Ord Tiddell}}</ref>
*[[Subject 4D668493X]] was an engineered killing and tracking machine created by Imperials.<ref name="Bounties to Die For">{{GamerCite|6|Bounties to Die For}}</ref>
*[[Voort saBinring]] was genetically altered to have extreme intelligence and mathematical skills.<ref name="X-Wing: Wraith Squadron">''[[X-Wing: Wraith Squadron]]''</ref>
*[[Rothana Heavy Engineering/Legends|Rothana Heavy Engineering]] sold a genetically modified [[gelagrub]] that was designed to not pupate into their beetle form.<ref name="Handbook">''[[Star Wars: Imperial Handbook: A Commander's Guide]]''</ref>
*The [[Oskan blood eater|oskan blood eaters]] were bioengineered by the [[Geneticist/Legends|genetic terrorist]] [[Zeta Magnus]].<ref name="SkyeWalkers">''[[SkyeWalkers: A Clone Wars Story]]''</ref>
